topic: Sukuna killed Gojo by copying the target-expansion idea from Mahoraga's second adaptation
title: Sukuna Beat Gojo By Stealing Mahoraga's Trick
description: Sukuna didn't break Gojo's Infinity, he borrowed a trick from Mahoraga's second adaptation to cut the world itself. Here's the detail that explains the whole Shinjuku ending. Was Gojo out-learned or just unlucky?
comment: Did Sukuna out-learn Gojo, or was Gojo doomed the moment Mahoraga showed up? Pick one.

lines.text: Sukuna didn't break Gojo's Infinity. He borrowed the answer from Mahoraga.

shot.fallback: dark curse king with tattoos facing white haired sorcerer

lines.text: And I think most fans missed how he did it.
Remember Mahoraga's first adaptation? It changed its cursed energy so the Infinity stopped working on it.

shot.fallback: eight handled sword divine general in shadow

lines.text: Sukuna couldn't copy that. His cursed energy just doesn't work that way.

shot.fallback: demon king watching a giant shikigami

lines.text: So he waited for the second adaptation.
That slash wasn't aimed at Gojo. It was aimed at the space around him.

shot.fallback: blade cutting through the air at a sorcerer

lines.text: Mahoraga stopped targeting a person and started targeting the whole world.

shot.fallback: white haired sorcerer losing an arm

lines.text: Sukuna took that idea and put it into his Dismantle.

shot.fallback: fingers pointing like a gun with slashes

lines.text: A slash that cuts the world itself, so the Infinity has nothing to stop.

shot.fallback: a slash splitting a city street in half

lines.text: Gojo wasn't outmatched. He got out-learned, by a shikigami he never beat.

shot.fallback: white haired sorcerer with a calm smile

lines.text: Which is why Sukuna didn't break Gojo's Infinity...

shot.fallback: glowing barrier around a white haired sorcerer

self_check.hook: contrarian claim naming Sukuna and Gojo in line 1
self_check.loop: last line ends mid-sentence into line 1 ('Sukuna didn't break Gojo's Infinity')
